title: Adding dissector for PDU-Transport
description:
This patch adds a new dissector for PDU-Transport. This is a very
simple protocol to transport CAN, FlexRay, LIN, and other PDUs.
It is typically used to transport legacy messages/PDUs over Ethernet.
The format is compatible to FDN and AUTOSAR.

Solves #17095

notes.body: Fuzz-Testing showed no bug.
Is this protocol documented somewhere, including the meaning of the ID field?

The only open specification I could find is rather bad to read:
https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/user_upload/standards/classic/20-11/AUTOSAR_SWS_SocketAdaptor.pdf
Section 7.3 explains the header format:

_[SWS_SoAd_00198]
The SoAd PDU header shall consist of a 4 byte ID field for
unique identification of the PDU at the receiver and a 4 byte length field specifying the data length of the PDU. Both in BigEndian byte order._
Let me add support for sub-dissectors

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1327/diffs?diff_id=131922265&start_sha=64dda2f08d3ae9a84fbc010db8904f9c66161689)

This is nice to see, we used a (slower) 60-line Lua dissector so far for this.

But the protocol might be better known as "SoAd"? Although "PDU Transport" better describes what it's doing...

I'd propose to keep the text in the Info column more concise, to more easily scan for the contents:
- Replace `PDU Transport (ID: 0x4eb)` by just `PDU:0x4eb` (potentially including length: `PDU:0x4eb[8]`)
- For known PDUs from user config: just show name (and length)

Is it required to pass the length via the struct to sub-dissectors? The length should be given by the sub-tvb anyway?

---

Some ideas to improve usefulness once the basic implementation is done:
- Add expected length field to PDU user config, adding warning expert info field if received length differs
- Add taps for statstics plugins / stats tree
- Support user defined signals configuration, added as dynamic protocol fields
- Add a "delta time since PDU last received" expert info field
- Add a "PDU content changed since PDU last received" expert info field (useful to filter only for real changes when PDUs are sent cyclically)

---

Lua variant:

```lua
local soad = Proto("soad", "AUTOSAR SocketAdapter")

local pf_messageid = ProtoField.new("Message ID", "soad.message", ftypes.UINT32, nil, base.HEX)
local pf_length = ProtoField.new("Length", "soad.length", ftypes.UINT32, nil, base.DEC)
local pf_payload = ProtoField.new("Payload", "soad.payload", ftypes.BYTES)
soad.fields = { pf_messageid, pf_length, pf_payload }

local expert_underflow = ProtoExpert.new("soad.underflow.expert", "Too little data available", expert.group.MALFORMED, expert.severity.ERROR)
soad.experts = { expert_underflow }

soad.dissector = function(tvb, pinfo, tree_root)
  pinfo.cols.protocol:set("SoAd")
  pinfo.cols.info:clear()

  local offset = 0
  repeat
    pinfo.cols.info:fence()
    local info_column_set = false

    if tvb:len() - offset < 8 then
      tree_root:add_proto_expert_info(expert_underflow)
      return
    end

    local messageid = tvb:range(offset, 4):uint()
    local length = tvb:range(offset + 4, 4):uint()
    local total_len = 4 + 4 + length
    local info_str = "PDU:"..string.format("0x%X", messageid).."["..length.."]"
    local root_tree_node_text = "AUTOSAR SocketAdapter, PDU: " .. string.format("0x%X", messageid) .. ", Len: " .. length

    if tvb:len() - offset < total_len then
      tree_root:add_proto_expert_info(expert_underflow)
      return
    end

    if not info_column_set then
      pinfo.cols.info:set(info_str .. " ")
      info_column_set = true
    else
      pinfo.cols.info:append(", "..info_str)
    end

    local tree = tree_root:add(soad, tvb:range(offset, total_len), root_tree_node_text)
    tree:add(pf_messageid, tvb:range(offset, 4))
    tree:add(pf_length, tvb:range(offset + 4, 4))

    local dtable = DissectorTable.get("soad.subdissector")
    local subdissector = dtable:get_dissector(tvb:range(offset, 4):uint())
    if subdissector then
      subdissector:call(tvb(offset + 8, length):tvb(), pinfo, tree)
    else
      tree:add(pf_payload, tvb:range(offset + 8, total_len - 8))
    end

    offset = offset + total_len
  until offset == tvb:len()
end

DissectorTable.new("soad.subdissector", "AUTOSAR SocketAdapter dissector", ftypes.UINT32)
```

I agree that Socket Adaptor would NOT be a better name since that is only the name of the a classic AUTOSAR module but not the protocol. And that is only one implementation of that protocol, there are many others as well.

I pass the length since all other protocols (e.g. CAN) do the same. I think that is a good idea since that could allow handling packets with bytes missing at the end in the future.

- The signal configuration is already in another merge request I am preparing. I split it since you can use it for CAN, FlexRay, and other ways to transport signals too. There we could check the expected length as well.
- "delta time since PDU last received", you can already do this by filtering. Isn't this enough?

- "Add taps for statistics plugins / stats tree"
--> What kind of statistics would be useful? 

- "Add a "PDU content changed since PDU last received" expert info field (useful to filter only for real changes when PDUs are sent cyclically)" --> The problem with this is that you receive the message on multiple links recorded (in the common case). So I there is a bigger problem to solve first. But maybe this is something that could be added!?

- Regarding the more concise column, I would prefer adding a name for the ID too. While this makes it a bit longer, it is much better to read. We could shorten the out put a bit but that looks really strange since the subdissectors might add something in between (e.g. NM).

> I pass the length since all other protocols (e.g. CAN) do the same. I think that is a good idea since that could allow handling packets with bytes missing at the end in the future.

This is handled in TVB's as well, through length vs reported_length.
Fixed in last commit.

> I shortened the text in the info column and added an expert info for truncated messages. The rest can be addressed in the signal dissector that will dissect the data.

Great. The patch works fine for me and my captures.

Some more cosmetic thoughts:
- Prevent the trailing `,` after the last PDU in the Info column
- To conform to other protocols, change the Packet Tree header from `PDU Transport Protocol (ID: 0xABCD)` to `PDU Transport Protocol, ID: 0xABCD, Len: 8`
- How about adding a `pdu_transport.payload` field into the PDU dissector tree, like the UDP/TCP dissectors do (but showing the actual bytes in the tree, since PDUs are typically rather short - or maybe for PDU lengths <= 32/64 bytes, and just the size info if bigger). That might make filtering easier compared to just filtering on `data`.
- If there is no subdissector for the PDU ID, the `pdu_transport.payload` field might make the separate generic `data` tree entry superfluous, making for a simpler tree especially for frames containing lots of PDUs.

> I agree that Socket Adaptor would NOT be a better name since that is only the name of the a classic AUTOSAR module but not the protocol.

Yes, "PDU Transport" is fitting.

However, maybe add a reference to AUTOSAR "Socket Adapter" and/or "SoAd" into the header comment and/or git commit message, so people searching for "Wireshark Socket Adapter" will hopefully find this patch and learn that they must use the protocol called "PDU Transport".

> The signal configuration is already in another merge request I am preparing. I split it since you can use it for CAN, FlexRay, and other ways to transport signals too. There we could check the expected length as well.

Ah, that's even better. Looking forward to it.

---

The rest is just a long-term wishlist:

> "delta time since PDU last received", you can already do this by filtering. Isn't this enough?

Sometimes you want to see this without refiltering your capture (which can take long for bigger files).
The TCP dissector has such extra fields.
It may also be interesting for filtering (like filtering for deltas greater than the expected cycle time)

> "Add taps for statistics plugins / stats tree" --> What kind of statistics would be useful?

A simple stats tree (`README.stats_tree`) plugin showing the counts, times, ... for each PDU ID would be a very nice start. Like the `Statistics >
Fixed the points except the "long-term wishlist". :)
Works great, would be happy to see this merged.

commits_data.message:
Adding dissector for PDU-Transport

This patch adds a new dissector for PDU-Transport. This is a very
simple protocol to transport CAN, FlexRay, LIN, and other PDUs.
It is typically used to transport legacy messages/PDUs over Ethernet.
The format is compatible to FDN and AUTOSAR.

Enabled AUTOSAR NM on top of the PDU Transport and fixed a few bugs
in AUTOSAR NM as well (length parsing).

Solves #17095
